clue.text: Contacted by phone caught express

parts.note: to have got something is to have caught it, as an illness or a ball
a through train is an express one, running straight to its destination

explanation.surface: Someone nabbed and sent off on a fast train.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting through on the telephone means making a connection and reaching the person called.

clue.text: Hollywood star discarding old clothes

indicators.note: throwing away, so a letter is dropped from the star's name

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish-born film star of Hollywood's golden age

explanation.surface: A film star throwing out an old wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a general word for dress or attire, a synonym for clothes.

clue.text: String round lamb cooked in meat dish?

indicators.note: one word goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: a tie is a string or cord for fastening

indicators.note: something cooked has been altered and prepared, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joint of lamb trussed with string and roasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'String' is a verb in the surface but gives a noun here; the question mark admits a timbale need not be meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a dish baked in a drum-shaped mould, often of minced meat or fish.

clue.text: Stay-at-home dad has unused hob worked out?

indicators.note: letters worked out are solved into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A father at home leaves the cooker untouched: is that how it works?
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out?' rearranges HAS UNUSED HOB into the answer; the surface suggests a dad who never cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who keeps house while his partner earns is the male counterpart of a housewife.

clue.text: Performing with US rock group, also inside awaiting a hearing

parts.note: on means on stage, performing
R.E.M., the American alternative rock band
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A musician on stage with an American band.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner held in custody before trial is in jail waiting for the court to sit.

clue.text: Grand circular stadium

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
round means circular in shape

explanation.surface: A magnificent round sports arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports ground is a stadium or pitch where matches are played.

clue.text: Experts: card sharks, primarily

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

indicators.note: first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Professional card cheats are the real experts.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are people who excel at something, top performers.

clue.text: Idle fancy about that man, English artist

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
him refers to a man already mentioned
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A daydream about some English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or impossible dream, after the mythical composite monster.

clue.text: Like some weapons Grant repositioned in land bordering the sea

indicators.note: one word goes in another, inside it

parts.note: the shore is the land along the edge of the sea

indicators.note: moved into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Grant moved his arms to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a person's name but is just the anagram fodder for 'repositioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Missiles meant for nearby targets are described as having a limited reach.

clue.text: American, after drink, quietly fell over in children's play area?

indicators.note: the American comes after the drink and the quiet piece

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: turned over, read the other way round

parts.note: a fell is a northern English hill or moor

explanation.surface: A drunk American quietly falling over in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns MOOR round. A fell is upland moor in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus room is a games room where children can play noisily; the question mark notes it is not only for them.

clue.text: Some crocodiles around open-air pool

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters run backwards
only some of the word is used, the letters sit inside it

explanation.surface: Crocodiles lurking around an outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ODIL from inside 'crocodiles' and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public outdoor swimming baths.

clue.text: In the loop, newly employed fellow minder

indicators.note: put to fresh use, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A new hire who looks after people knows what is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in the loop means knowing the latest news, being well briefed.

clue.text: Come to watch

definitions.meaning: to regain consciousness, rouse from sleep
a vigil kept over a dead body

explanation.surface: Arrive to keep an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake is to rouse from sleep; a wake is a vigil kept beside the dead.

clue.text: Finely chop heart for pie filling

parts.note: to mince is to cut into very small pieces
the meat of something is its core or essence

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: chop the heart small for a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat, a mix of dried fruit and spices, fills Christmas mince pies.

clue.text: Suffering in Florida during a romance

indicators.note: Florida comes during, inside, the other words

parts.note: a romance is a novel, a work of fiction
FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A love affair in Florida turns painful.
explanation.definitionFit: An affliction is a cause of pain or distress, a trouble endured.

clue.text: Often visit common

definitions.meaning: to go regularly to a place, as a haunt

explanation.surface: Going regularly to the village green.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to haunt a place; as an adjective it means happening often.

clue.text: Recalled a better article about large animal

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: An improved write-up about a big beast, withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns A CAP into PACA; the article goes next to ('about') L for size large, giving AL in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpaca is a South American relative of the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Quiet leisurely walk ending in horrendous fiasco

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an amble is a slow stroll

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A peaceful stroll that ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles is a scene of total disorder, a complete mess.

clue.text: Basin and toilet with a nasty smell

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A smelly washroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavabo is a washbasin, originally for ritual hand-washing at Mass.

clue.text: Condiment given a shaking, right?

indicators.note: letters given a shake are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A seasoning bottle being shaken: correct?
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid used as a seasoning, with salt on chips.

clue.text: Article about family's philosophy

indicators.note: one word goes about, around, the other

parts.note: an article is an item or thing
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a family's outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is not A or THE here: it means an object, THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's thinking is their way of reasoning, their outlook or philosophy.

clue.text: Ship heading off with Spanish aunt showing a tendency to do nothing

indicators.note: with its head, the first letter, taken off

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship
tia is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: A ship sets off carrying a lazy Spanish aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is resistance to change or action, sluggishness.

clue.text: Pottery in horse-drawn Russian carriage

definitions.meaning: a studio pottery workshop in St Ives, Cornwall, known for 1960s-70s ceramics
a sled or carriage pulled by three horses abreast

explanation.surface: Ceramics carried in a Russian sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a proper name: Troika Pottery worked in St Ives, Cornwall, in the 1960s and 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: the Cornish studio and the three-horse vehicle from Russia.

clue.text: Study a French instrument in puzzle

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
un is French for a
a drum is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Practising a French instrument is a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a riddle or difficult problem.

clue.text: Free duck and swan

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A duck and a swan, no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means unrestricted, available or unoccupied.

clue.text: Examine small tin

parts.note: a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: Inspect a little tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over closely or inspect.

clue.text: I try to describe a villainous Shakespearean character

indicators.note: to describe here means to draw round, so the words enclose a letter

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: An attempt to portray a Shakespeare villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describe' is used in its geometry sense of drawing a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Othello.

clue.text: Sensitive police officer unlikely to claim after pressure applied

indicators.note: pressure comes after the officer

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the letters are put in an improbable, altered order

explanation.surface: A tactful officer who wouldn't claim anything once pressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges TO CLAIM to LOMATIC; 'applied' just says pressure is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomatic means tactful and careful of others' feelings.

clue.text: Boring student starts to name each ruddy dog!

indicators.note: the starts, the first letters, of the next four words

explanation.surface: A dull pupil insists on naming every dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is a studious, socially awkward person, a swot.

clue.text: Protested heatedly, as Adam and Eve did?

definitions.meaning: made a loud fuss or uproar
Adam and Eve brought up Cain, their first son

explanation.surface: A furious protest, the way the first parents did.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means caused trouble noisily; literally Adam and Eve reared their son Cain.
